questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q01

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | foundation

What is decolonization?

generalfeedback.text: Formal sovereignty could expand even while foreign influence continued.

answer.text: The process by which colonial territories gain autonomy or political independence

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q02

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | foundation

Satyagraha refers to

generalfeedback.text: Satyagraha informed Gandhi’s approach to resistance.

answer.text: Gandhi’s concept of nonviolent resistance grounded in truth and moral force

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q03

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | foundation

Nonalignment meant

generalfeedback.text: Nonaligned states pursued their own policies.

answer.text: formal membership in both Cold War blocs
avoiding formal alignment with either bloc while retaining independent positions

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q04

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | foundation

What was apartheid?

generalfeedback.text: Apartheid was a state-created political and legal system.

answer.text: South Africa’s system of institutionalized racial segregation and white-minority rule

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q05

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | foundation

In this lesson, partition means

generalfeedback.text: British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan in 1947.

answer.text: division of territory into separate political units

generalfeedback.text: The dates show varied regional timing.

Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q07

What does the map clarify?

generalfeedback.text: The territorial arrangement and two-way migration were complex.

answer.text: Pakistan initially consisted of western and eastern territories separated by India

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q08

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

“Civil disobedience becomes a sacred duty when the State becomes lawless or corrupt.”

M. K. Gandhi, Young India, 1930. Short historical excerpt.

What strategy does the excerpt support?

generalfeedback.text: The statement supports principled nonviolent resistance.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q09

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

“Civil disobedience becomes a sacred duty when the State becomes lawless or corrupt.”

M. K. Gandhi, Young India, 1930. Short historical excerpt.

Which limitation is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: Leadership evidence must be contextualized with movements and conditions.

answer.text: A leader’s statement does not represent every participant or all causes of independence

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q10

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

“Seek ye first the political kingdom and all things shall be added unto you.”

Kwame Nkrumah, independence-era political slogan.

What goal is emphasized?

generalfeedback.text: The slogan prioritizes political independence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q11

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

Path comparison
CaseStrategy and contextOutcome
India/PakistanMass politics, nonviolent civil disobedience, negotiation; repression and partition violenceIndependence and partition, 1947
GhanaNationalist organization and negotiationIndependence, 1957
KenyaLand conflict, protest, Mau Mau armed resistance, detention, negotiationIndependence, 1963
AlgeriaFLN armed struggle against French settler colonialismIndependence, 1962

Which conclusion is supported?

generalfeedback.text: Decolonization followed varied paths.

answer.text: India/Ghana and Kenya/Algeria demonstrate different mixes of negotiation, mass politics, and armed conflict

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q12

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

Interacting causes of decolonization
World War II weakened empiresNationalist mobilizationEconomic costs
Colonial resistanceAnti-imperial ideasInternational/UN pressure
Colonial soldiers’ participationCold War contextImperial political decisions

Which conclusion is best supported?

generalfeedback.text: The network rejects single-cause explanations.

answer.text: Global and local pressures interacted to weaken colonial empires

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q13

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | interpretation

“I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities.”

Nelson Mandela, Rivonia Trial statement, April 20, 1964; Nelson Mandela Foundation transcript.

What democratic goal is expressed?

generalfeedback.text: The statement articulates political equality and democracy.

1957Ghana
1962Algeria

“I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities.”

Nelson Mandela, Rivonia Trial statement, April 20, 1964; Nelson Mandela Foundation transcript.

generalfeedback.text: The case is comparative democratic reform.

answer.text: South Africa’s 1994 transition was later democratic reform against apartheid, not a 1940s transfer from a European colony

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q17

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Which claim avoids a great-person explanation?

generalfeedback.text: Leaders matter within broader movements and institutions.

answer.text: Gandhi was important within mass movements, organizations, wartime change, negotiations, other leaders, and British decisions

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q18

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Which explanation is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: The process was multi-causal and politically complex.

answer.text: Competing nationalisms, negotiation, colonial structures, representation concerns, and communal tension interacted

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q19

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Path comparison
CaseStrategy and contextOutcome
India/PakistanMass politics, nonviolent civil disobedience, negotiation; repression and partition violenceIndependence and partition, 1947
GhanaNationalist organization and negotiationIndependence, 1957
KenyaLand conflict, protest, Mau Mau armed resistance, detention, negotiationIndependence, 1963

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q20

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Which statement best preserves agency during the Cold War?

generalfeedback.text: Cold War context did not erase local interests.

answer.text: New states were only U.S. or Soviet pieces
New states pursued national goals, sometimes through nonalignment, while accepting or rejecting outside aid

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q21

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Why did independence not guarantee stable democracy?

generalfeedback.text: Inherited conditions and later choices interacted.

answer.text: States faced inherited borders and institutions, economic pressures, social divisions, Cold War pressure, and consequential local choices

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q22

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

“Seek ye first the political kingdom and all things shall be added unto you.”

Kwame Nkrumah, independence-era political slogan.

Which evaluation is balanced?

generalfeedback.text: Historical significance can include achievement and limitation.

answer.text: Nkrumah helped lead significant independence and Pan-African politics, while later centralization complicates his legacy

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q23

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

“I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities.”

Nelson Mandela, Rivonia Trial statement, April 20, 1964; Nelson Mandela Foundation transcript.

Which explanation is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: South African transition was multi-causal.

answer.text: Internal resistance, ANC organization, international pressure, sanctions, economic conditions, de Klerk, Mandela, and negotiation interacted

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L04_Q24

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Path comparison
CaseStrategy and contextOutcome
India/PakistanMass politics, nonviolent civil disobedience, negotiation; repression and partition violenceIndependence and partition, 1947
GhanaNationalist organization and negotiationIndependence, 1957
KenyaLand conflict, protest, Mau Mau armed resistance, detention, negotiationIndependence, 1963
AlgeriaFLN armed struggle against French settler colonialismIndependence, 1962

Which CER is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: The response connects specific evidence to a comparative claim.

answer.text: Claim: imperial response shaped conflict. Evidence: France fought to retain settler-colonial Algeria. Reasoning: fewer negotiated openings intensified armed struggle.
Claim: all paths were identical. Evidence: outcomes differed.
Claim: leaders acted alone. Evidence: movements appear in every row.
Claim: violence was absent. Evidence: Kenya and Algeria.

Alignment: MLA.WH.DEC.01–02 | application

Interacting causes of decolonization
World War II weakened empiresNationalist mobilizationEconomic costs
Colonial resistanceAnti-imperial ideasInternational/UN pressure
Colonial soldiers’ participationCold War contextImperial political decisions
Path comparison
CaseStrategy and contextOutcome
India/PakistanMass politics, nonviolent civil disobedience, negotiation; repression and partition violenceIndependence and partition, 1947
GhanaNationalist organization and negotiationIndependence, 1957
KenyaLand conflict, protest, Mau Mau armed resistance, detention, negotiationIndependence, 1963

generalfeedback.text: The synthesis integrates common causes and differing outcomes.

answer.text: Shared postwar pressures weakened empire, while different institutions, movements, divisions, strategies, and imperial responses produced different paths
